Chapter Eight: The Power and Peril of Influence
You know, as life moves forward, we start to wonder—just how much can we really influence the world around us? And, at the same time, how much does the world shape us in return? That urge to make a difference, to leave your mark—it’s powerful. But living through times of upheaval teaches us something tough: influence is almost never as simple as it seems.
Think about those big decisions made in the halls of power. Maybe they started with the best intentions, but the results? Often, they’re unpredictable. A well-meaning reform might set off a chain of unexpected problems. And sometimes, even the boldest new idea is met with a shrug—or worse, outright resistance. Society is this massive, complicated machine, and honestly, no one person can steer it alone.
Imagine this: after a long, exhausting day of meetings, there’s a public servant sitting alone in his study. He’s replaying everything in his mind—the arguments, the alliances, the hard work. And still, the results are a mixed bag. Some changes stick, others just fade away. That’s when it hits him: real influence isn’t about controlling everything. It’s about showing up, being part of the bigger conversation, and knowing that outcomes will always have a little uncertainty built in.
The same idea shows up in our day-to-day relationships. We want to help, to guide, to protect the people we care about. But there are no guarantees. Kids grow up and make their own choices. Friends drift apart, or sometimes surprise us with how strong they are. And, looking back, it’s usually not the grand gestures that matter most. It’s the quiet example we set—the way we live, how we listen, and how we respond to what life throws at us.
Over time, chasing influence starts to feel different. The real goal isn’t shaping the world exactly how you want it. It’s about engaging honestly, offering what you can, and accepting there will always be things outside your control. Meaning comes not just from the results, but from the effort—the way you show up and try, even when you can’t predict the outcome.
